CONCORDIA'S THURSDAY REPORT, THREE ISSUES 1990-1992
The Seaman awards, in the university's own newspaper

Found 2026-09-07 by the accounted sweep of rma-concordia-publications (p_479).
None previously in sources.json; the wiki cites a 2001 Thursday Report for
Seaman and nothing earlier. One text file each, checked.

  1990-11-15  Vol. 15 No. 11   117,204 chars
  1991-06-06  Vol. 15 No. 30   175,684 chars
  1992-03-19  Vol. 16 No. 21   112,668 chars

===============================================================================
15 NOVEMBER 1990 — "FIVE LEADERSHIP AWARDS", AND A LINE THAT CLOSES A LOOP
===============================================================================

From Mike Shahin's report of the first Concordia award presentation:

  "Ross Seaman was a graduate of Sir George Williams University and a part-time
  faculty member of Concordia's APSS and Leisure Studies Departments. HE
  ORIGINATED THE DAWSON COLLEGE COMMUNITY RECREATION AND LEADERSHIP PROGRAMME
  AND WAS AN ADVISER TO THE YMCA FELLOWSHIP STAFF. His life's work involved
  helping people feel good about themselves. 'No matter who (Seaman) was with,'
  APSS Professor Dick McDonald said before the award presentation last week,
  'they always came out of the experience more upbeat than when they went in.'

  Seaman died in 1987. FIVE LEADERSHIP AWARDS HAVE BEEN CREATED IN HIS NAME to
  be presented annually. TWO AWARDS ARE PRESENTED TO CONCORDIA STUDENTS IN THE
  APSS AND LEISURE STUDIES PROGRAMMES. THE OTHER AWARDS ARE PRESENTED TO
  STUDENTS AT DAWSON, THOSE INVOLVED WITH THE YM/WCA AND WITH KAMP KANAWANA."

The photograph caption names those present: "APSS Professor Dick McDonald, MRS.
MARGARET SEAMAN, winner [name] and APSS Chair Richard Cawley gather at the award
presentation." Photo by Owen Egan.

THREE THINGS, AND THE FIRST IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST.

(a) "AN ADVISER TO THE YMCA FELLOWSHIP STAFF." The Fellowship is the Montreal
    YMCA's Training Fellowship, documented in this project earlier the same day
    from Sir George Williams yearbooks of 1942 and 1943 — a paid apprenticeship
    in the Association secretaryship, worked in the branches, with enrolment at
    the college as its academic half. Concordia's own obituary of Seaman says he
    "attended Sir George as a YMCA Fellowship Secretary" in the 1940s. SO HE
    CAME THROUGH THE FELLOWSHIP AND LATER ADVISED ITS STAFF. The scheme that
    made him is a scheme he went back and helped run.

(b) "HE ORIGINATED THE DAWSON COLLEGE COMMUNITY RECREATION AND LEADERSHIP
    PROGRAMME." wiki/people/a-ross-seaman.md has him becoming "teacher and
    chairperson of the CRLT Department at Dawson" in 1974. "Originated" is a
    stronger claim than "chaired", and it comes from his own university's
    newspaper reporting on an award in his name — a friendly source, so the
    claim is recorded as theirs rather than adopted flat.

(c) FIVE AWARDS, NOT ONE. Everything this project holds treats the Seaman fund
    as a single scholarship. It was five annual awards: two at Concordia (one
    each in APSS and Leisure Studies), one at Dawson, one through the YM/WCA,
    one through Kamp Kanawana. That also explains the 1995-96 calendar's plural
    "A. Ross Seaman Memorial SCHOLARSHIPS", which had looked like loose wording.
    NOTE "YM/WCA" — the YWCA is in it too, which no other source here says.

===============================================================================
6 JUNE 1991 — A SIXTH CONSTITUENCY, AND THE CUP MOVES
===============================================================================

  "The A. Ross Seaman Award for outstanding community leadership was presented
  at the 'LEISURE IN THE 21ST CENTURY' seminar in March. The award went to Peter
  Clark, a student in Leisure Studies. THOUGH IT WAS THE FIRST TIME THAT THE
  AWARD WAS GIVEN TO A STUDENT IN THAT DEPARTMENT, the award is offered to
  groups that the late Ross Seaman was involved in, such as the YMCA, Kamp
  Kanawana, Concordia's Department of Applied Social Science, as well as Dawson
  College AND IN HIS HOME COMMUNITY OF PRESCOTT-RUSSELL. Clark said that
  although he never met Seaman, he knew how much he had done to help youth.
  Clark is actively involved with the Boy Scouts and outdoor education
  programmes.

  THE ROSS SEAMAN CUP, an annual 'friendly' competition, WAS HELD IN MAY AT THE
  BEACONSFIELD RECREATION CENTRE."

PRESCOTT-RUSSELL is the united counties of eastern Ontario containing VANKLEEK
HILL, which wiki/people/a-ross-seaman.md already names as his home community and
as the site of one of the five memorial scholarships. This names the county, and
shows the home community was a constituency of the award scheme itself rather
than a separate local memorial.

AND THE CUP MOVED. Held in MAY 1991 at the Beaconsfield Recreation Centre;
held in MARCH 1992 at Loyola. So it was not fixed to a month or a place.

===============================================================================
19 MARCH 1992 — THE CUP'S OWN INVITATION, WITH A THEME
===============================================================================

  "FRIDAY, MARCH 20 1992. A. Ross Seaman Memorial Cup. TO THE STUDENTS OF
  CONCORDIA UNIVERSITY LEISURE STUDIES AND A.P.S.S., DAWSON COLLEGE C.R.L.T. AND
  YMCA CAMP KANAWANA. You are invited to participate in this year's A. Ross
  Seaman Memorial Cup, 'RECREATION AND LEISURE, A DOOR TO THE FUTURE.' This is a
  one-day mission to raise money for the scholarship fund, learn leadership
  development and have a great time. The day will kick off with an INTERGALACTIC
  GAME OF SPACEBALL and includes other OUT-OF-THIS-WORLD EVENTS, such as variety
  show, t-shirts, free dinner, an auction and awards. Time: 2:30 p.m. Location:
  Loyola Campus - Athletics Complex (7200 Sherbrooke St. W.)"

The Link's notice of the same event, found earlier today, gives the venue as
7141 Sherbrooke St. W. and this one 7200. A small discrepancy in a street number
for the same complex, recorded and not resolved.

===============================================================================
A NOTE ON NAMES
===============================================================================

The 1990 article names and describes its award winner in some personal detail
and the 1991 piece names its own. Consistent with the decision registered as
r_0006 on the 2007 bursary booklet, THE INSTITUTIONAL FACTS ARE TAKEN AND THE
WINNERS' PERSONAL CIRCUMSTANCES ARE NOT REPRODUCED IN THE WIKI. Peter Clark is
named because "the first time the award was given to a student in that
department" is a fact about the award rather than about him, and because the
same name appears in the 2007 honour roll, which confirms that roster's
accuracy. The 1990 winner is referred to without her name and without her
biography.
